**Kat:**

Write me a script that will rename files based on file names in a .csv in R

**Claude:**

I've written the script as `rename_files.R`. It assumes a CSV with two columns, `old_name` and `new_name`, with file extensions included in both.

To use it, set `csv_path` and `file_dir` in the settings block at the top. If your column headers differ, change `old_col` and `new_col` to match.

It defaults to a dry run, which prints the planned renames without touching anything. Once the preview looks right, set `dry_run <- FALSE` and run it again.

It also checks a few things before renaming, so a bad CSV doesn't wreck your files:
- Files listed in the CSV but missing from the folder are skipped with a warning.
- Duplicate new names in the CSV stop the script.
- New names that already exist in the folder are skipped, so nothing gets overwritten.

If your CSV uses a different layout, such as a prefix or pattern instead of full new names, let me know and I'll adjust it.

:::

### Manual Data Cleaning

When looking at the datasheets, I notice the following things:

 - 2004, 2005, and 2008 are all the same format.
 
 - 2008 says it may be mis-typed, so that needs to be noted in the spreadsheet.
 
 - 2026 consists of three separate excel sheets with very different formats.
 
There are a few sheets in one of the most recent year's documents (2026) that need to be deleted as they will not import correctly into R or contain data that lacks identifying information. These are detailed below:

 1. 2026b_OPIHI_data - removed sheets: "LIMU PRESSES", "QUADRAT PT INTERCEPT (EXAMPLE)", and "Sheet9". The first one was removed due to it being a photograph of limu pressings with no other data. The second is example data from another year. The third one (Sheet9) was removed as it contains temperature data with no associated location data to group with.

 
### Manual Redaction (2004, 2005, 2008) and AI compilation

I will be redacting names and other sensitive data from 2004a, 2005a, and 2008a before using AI to help compile it. I have changed coordinates, site names, and removed any identifying information.

Now I will use AI to write me a script that will pull the information and join these three files together into the correct format.

**Claude:**

I've written the script, `combine_opihi_data.R`, but I couldn't run it because R isn't installed in my sandbox. I checked the workbook layouts and worked out the expected row counts in Python instead, so your first run is the real test.

**How it works**
- Each workbook holds several surveys side by side. A survey starts wherever row 1 says "Date", and there are 20 across your three files (3 in 2004, 16 in 2005, 1 in 2008).
- For each survey it reads the metadata (date, times, location, lat/lon, school, transect info), then the quadrat labels and the organism counts.
- It splits labels like `transect-1 quadrat-6 at point 6.50` into separate `transect`, `quadrat` and `point_m` columns.
- It skips the "TOTALS:" section under each survey, since that can be recomputed from the raw counts.

**Output:** a tidy CSV with one row per organism per quadrat. The columns are:
- `source_file`, `sheet`
- `date`, `start_time`, `stop_time`
- `location`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `school`
- `n_transect_lines`, `transect_line_length`
- `point_spacing`, `point_spacing_m`, `quadrats_per_transect`
- `transect`, `quadrat`, `point_m`
- `organism`, `count`

**To use it**
1. Put the script in the same folder as the three `.xlsx` files (or change `data_dir` at the top).
2. Run `install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "purrr", "readr", "tibble"))` once.
3. Run the script. It writes `combined_data1.csv` to your working directory.

**Things to know**
- **Blank cells:** by default only recorded counts are kept, which should give about 1,762 rows (247 + 1,299 + 216). Setting `drop_empty_cells <- FALSE` keeps every organism and quadrat combination, with blanks written as 0, for 9,806 rows. That assumes a blank means "not seen", so check that matches your protocol.
- **Latitude and longitude:** the source files only store whole degrees (e.g. 21, -159), so the CSV does too.
- **Transect length units:** the workbooks don't give them, so that column is just called `transect_line_length`.
- **2008 sheet name:** the sheet is named "OPIHI data 2008 (might be mis-t…", which hints at a data-entry doubt. I used the data as-is.

If your row count differs from the numbers above, tell me what you get and I'll track it down.


:::


```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# combine_opihi_data.R
#
# Combines the OPIHI survey workbooks (2004a, 2005a, 2008a, ...) into one
# tidy ("long") CSV: one row per organism x quadrat, with the survey
# metadata (date, location, lat/lon, etc.) repeated on every row.
#
# Each workbook has several survey blocks laid out SIDE BY SIDE. A block
# starts in the column where row 1 says "Date":
#   rows 1-11 : metadata (label in the block's first column, value next to it)
#   row  13   : "Organisms" + one label per quadrat
#               ("transect-1 quadrat-1 at point 0.50")
#   row  14+  : organism name + counts, until the first blank organism cell
# Anything below that (the "TOTALS:" section) is ignored, because it can be
# recomputed from the raw counts.
#
# Requires: readxl, dplyr, purrr, readr, tibble
#   install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "purrr", "readr", "tibble"))
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)

# ---- Settings -----------------------------------------------------
data_dir   <- here("OPIHI_Project", "Data", "2004_2005_2008_notredacted")  # folder containing the .xlsx files
file_regex <- "_OPIHI_data\\.xlsx$"  # which files to combine
out_file   <- here("OPIHI_Project", "Outputs", "combined_data1.csv")

# Blank cells mean "organism not recorded in that quadrat".
#   TRUE  = keep only recorded counts (smaller file)
#   FALSE = keep every organism x quadrat combination, blanks written as 0
drop_empty_cells <- TRUE
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# Safely get one cell from the raw sheet (returns NA if empty/out of range)
get_cell <- function(m, r, c) {
  if (r > nrow(m) || c > ncol(m) || c < 1) return(NA)
  v <- m[[c]][[r]]
  if (is.null(v) || length(v) == 0) NA else v
}

fmt_date <- function(x) if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) format(x, "%Y-%m-%d") else as.character(x)
fmt_time <- function(x) if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) format(x, "%H:%M")    else as.character(x)

quadrat_pattern <- "^transect-([0-9]+) quadrat-([0-9]+) at point ([0-9.]+)$"

# Parse one survey block (columns `start` to `end`) into a long tibble
parse_block <- function(m, start, end, source_file, sheet_name) {

  # --- metadata (rows 1-11), looked up by label so row order doesn't matter
  meta_rows <- 1:11
  meta <- map(meta_rows, ~ get_cell(m, .x, start + 1))
  names(meta) <- map_chr(meta_rows, ~ as.character(get_cell(m, .x, start)))
  num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))

  # --- quadrat columns: those with a label in row 13
  header_row <- 13
  qcols   <- (start + 1):end
  qlabels <- map_chr(qcols, ~ as.character(get_cell(m, header_row, .x)))
  keep    <- !is.na(qlabels)
  qcols   <- qcols[keep]
  qlabels <- qlabels[keep]

  # --- organism rows: from row 14 until the first blank organism name
  r <- header_row + 1
  org_rows <- integer(0)
  while (r <= nrow(m) && !is.na(get_cell(m, r, start))) {
    org_rows <- c(org_rows, r)
    r <- r + 1
  }
  if (length(org_rows) == 0 || length(qcols) == 0) return(NULL)

  # --- every organism x quadrat combination
  grid <- expand.grid(i = seq_along(org_rows), j = seq_along(qcols))
  out <- tibble(
    organism = map_chr(grid$i, ~ as.character(get_cell(m, org_rows[.x], start))),
    label    = qlabels[grid$j],
    count    = map_dbl(seq_len(nrow(grid)),
                       ~ num(get_cell(m, org_rows[grid$i[.x]], qcols[grid$j[.x]])))
  )

  ok <- grepl(quadrat_pattern, out$label)
  out <- out %>%
    mutate(
      transect = suppressWarnings(as.integer(ifelse(ok, sub(quadrat_pattern, "\\1", label), NA))),
      quadrat  = suppressWarnings(as.integer(ifelse(ok, sub(quadrat_pattern, "\\2", label), NA))),
      point_m  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ifelse(ok, sub(quadrat_pattern, "\\3", label), NA)))
    )

  # --- attach metadata
  out %>%
    mutate(
      source_file           = source_file,
      sheet                 = sheet_name,
      date                  = fmt_date(meta[["Date"]]),
      start_time            = fmt_time(meta[["Start Time"]]),
      stop_time             = fmt_time(meta[["Stop Time"]]),
      location              = as.character(meta[["Location"]]),
      latitude              = num(meta[["latitude"]]),
      longitude             = num(meta[["longitude"]]),
      school                = as.character(meta[["School"]]),
      n_transect_lines      = num(meta[["Number of Transect Lines"]]),
      transect_line_length  = num(meta[["Length of Transect Lines"]]),
      point_spacing         = as.character(meta[["Point Spacing"]]),
      point_spacing_m       = parse_number(as.character(meta[["Point Spacing"]])),
      quadrats_per_transect = num(meta[["Number of Quadrats per transect"]])
    ) %>%
    select(source_file, sheet, date, start_time, stop_time, location,
           latitude, longitude, school, n_transect_lines, transect_line_length,
           point_spacing, point_spacing_m, quadrats_per_transect,
           transect, quadrat, point_m, organism, count)
}

# Parse every survey block on one sheet
parse_sheet <- function(path, sheet_name) {
  # col_types = "list" keeps each cell's native type (dates, times, numbers, text)
  m <- read_excel(path, sheet = sheet_name, col_names = FALSE,
                  col_types = "list", .name_repair = "minimal")

  # A block starts wherever row 1 says "Date"
  starts <- which(map_lgl(seq_len(ncol(m)),
                          ~ identical(as.character(get_cell(m, 1, .x)), "Date")))
  if (length(starts) == 0) {
    warning("No survey blocks found in ", basename(path), " [", sheet_name, "]")
    return(NULL)
  }
  ends <- c(starts[-1] - 1, ncol(m))

  map2_dfr(starts, ends, ~ parse_block(m, .x, .y, basename(path), sheet_name))
}

# ---- Run ----------------------------------------------------------
files <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = file_regex, full.names = TRUE)
if (length(files) == 0) stop("No files matching '", file_regex, "' found in '", data_dir, "'")
message("Found ", length(files), " file(s):\n  ", paste(basename(files), collapse = "\n  "))

combined <- map_dfr(sort(files), function(f) {
  map_dfr(excel_sheets(f), ~ parse_sheet(f, .x))
})

if (drop_empty_cells) {
  combined <- filter(combined, !is.na(count))
} else {
  combined <- mutate(combined, count = coalesce(count, 0))
}

combined <- arrange(combined, date, location, transect, quadrat, organism)

write_csv(combined, out_file, na = "")
message("Wrote ", nrow(combined), " rows x ", ncol(combined), " columns to ", out_file)
```

The new script is `combine_opihi_data2.R`, and it writes `combined_data2.csv`. As before, I couldn't run it because R isn't installed in my sandbox, so I checked the workbooks and counted expected rows in Python instead.

**These files needed a new script.** The 2026 workbooks use a different layout from the first batch.
- **2026a and 2026c** share one template. A Metadata sheet has one row per survey. A transect sheet has one organism or substrate per point. A Quadrat sheet has one row per quadrat and one column per organism.
- **2026b** is a different, class-compiled workbook. It has transect points by group and quadrat totals by group.

**Output:** `combined_data2.csv` has one row per observation, with these columns:
- `source_file`, `sheet`, `record_type`
- `date`, `location`, `data_entry_by`, `group`
- `transect`, `transect_point`, `position_m`, `quadrat_location_m`
- `category`, `organism`, `count`
- `quadrat_total_points`, `notes`

`record_type` tells you what each row is:
- `transect_point`: one transect point, with `count` = 1.
- `quadrat_points`: a per-quadrat count (2026a and 2026c).
- `quadrat_group_total`: a count totalled over a whole group's survey (2026b has no per-quadrat detail).

**Row counts to check against (R's `nrow`):** about 2,000 rows by default. With `drop_empty_cells <- FALSE` it's 12,873. Per file, the default is:
- 2026a: 98 transect rows and 1,164 quadrat rows.
- 2026b: 246 transect rows and 113 quadrat rows.
- 2026c: 105 transect rows and 274 quadrat rows.

**One extra file:** the script also writes `combined_metadata2.csv` (8 survey rows from 2026a and 2026c). I kept the metadata separate because I couldn't safely attach it to each observation. For example, 2026a has two metadata rows for 1/24 at ʻEwa Beach, with different team leaders. If you'd rather not have it, delete the last few lines of the script.

**Things I handled or left alone**
- **Stray template blocks:** the 2026a and 2026c transect sheets have two copies of the quadrat template pasted below the real data. Those rows (including leftover 2025 "Madison Armstrong" data) are ignored.
- **2026b contains placeholder or demo content:** names like "fake name1", "jgvfb" and "asdf", and a "DEMO DATA ANALYSIS" section. I included its observation tables, and you can filter them out with `source_file`. Its transect dates (4/20 and 5/4/26) come from the workbook's titles and are set in `b_transect_dates` at the top of the script.
- **Missing dates:** 13 transect rows in 2026a (Lēʻahi, transect 3) have no date, and I left them blank rather than guess. One 2026a quadrat row has "Gigi" typed in the date cell, so its date is blank too. One 2026c quadrat row has no date, location or transect, but it does have counts, so I kept it.
- **Likely date errors in 2026a:** some consecutive transect points on Mauliola transects 2 and 4 have dates that step up one day at a time (1/25 through 1/31). That looks like an auto-fill mistake. I left the dates as entered.
- **Unnamed column:** the quadrat column 58 in both files has a header of just "3" (all zeros), so it shows up as `organism` = "3".
- **Organism names:** these are free text and not standardized ("Padina", "Padina Sp.", "Padina spp"). The script trims whitespace but doesn't merge variants, since that needs your judgment.
- **Renamed columns:** the 2026a and 2026c quadrat sheets rename two columns (Echinometra vs "Urchin - Echinometra", Sea Star vs Brittle Star). They are kept as two separate organism names.

Once you've run it, let me know if your counts differ from those above and I'll track down the cause.

Cause found: `read_excel()` silently drops leading empty columns. Column A of the 2026b "QUADRAT PT INTERCEPT" sheet is empty, so every column shifted left by one, the header search found nothing, and the loop got a missing row number. I'm anchoring all reads at cell A1 so positions always match the spreadsheet.

I'll also add a clear error message in case a header can't be found in future.

I've fixed it in the updated `combine_opihi_data2.R`.

**Cause:** `read_excel()` quietly skips leading empty columns. Column A of the 2026b "QUADRAT PT INTERCEPT" sheet is completely empty, so every column shifted one to the left. The script then couldn't find the "Organism/Substrate" header in column B, got a missing row number, and crashed in the `while` loop.

**Fix:** every sheet is now read from cell A1 (`range = cell_limits(c(1, 1), c(NA, NA))`), so cell positions always match the spreadsheet. I also added a clear error message, in case a header ever can't be found.

Re-run the whole script. The expected counts are unchanged, at about 2,000 rows by default and 12,873 with `drop_empty_cells <- FALSE`. Since I can't run R here, other errors could still turn up. If you get another, paste it here and I'll fix it.

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# combine_opihi_data2.R
#
# Combines the 2026 OPIHI workbooks (2026a, 2026b, 2026c) into one tidy
# ("long") CSV, combined_data2.csv, plus a small companion file with the
# survey-level metadata (combined_metadata2.csv).
#
# These workbooks use a DIFFERENT layout from the 2004/2005/2008 files:
#
#  2026a / 2026c  (same template)
#    "Metadata"                      one row per survey (-> metadata file)
#    "Transect" / "Transect Point    one row per transect point, with the
#       Intercept"                   organism/substrate under that point
#    "Quadrat PtCounts"              one row per quadrat, one column per
#                                    organism (row 1 = category, row 2 = name)
#    The Transect sheet also contains two stray copies of the quadrat
#    template pasted below the real data (starting at a row whose column A
#    is blank-ish text or "Date"); everything from there down is ignored.
#
#  2026b  (class-compiled workbook; contains placeholder names and demo data)
#    "TRANSECT PT INTERCEPT (420)"   4/20/26 point intercepts, one column
#    "TRANSECT PT INTERCEPT (54)"    5/4/26  point intercepts, per group
#    "QUADRAT PT INTERCEPT"          organism x group TOTALS for each date
#    "GROUPS", "Total TRANSECT" and the analysis columns are summaries or
#    instructions, not observations, so they are not read.
#
# Output columns (record_type says which kind of row it is):
#   transect_point       one point on a transect; count = 1 (one hit)
#   quadrat_points       number of the quadrat's points that landed on the
#                        organism (2026a/c: per quadrat)
#   quadrat_group_total  same, but totalled over a group's whole survey
#                        (2026b only; no per-quadrat detail exists)
#
# Requires: readxl, dplyr, purrr, readr, tibble
#   install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "purrr", "readr", "tibble"))
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)

# ---- Settings -----------------------------------------------------
data_dir   <- here("OPIHI_Project", "Data")
files      <- c("2026a_OPIHI_data.xlsx", "2026b_OPIHI_data.xlsx", "2026c_OPIHI_data.xlsx")
out_file   <- here("OPIHI_Project", "Outputs", "combined_data2.csv")
meta_file  <- here("OPIHI_Project", "Outputs", "combined_metadata2.csv")

# Blank quadrat cells mean "organism not recorded in that quadrat".
#   TRUE  = keep only recorded counts (smaller file)
#   FALSE = keep every organism for every quadrat/group that has data,
#           blanks written as 0
drop_empty_cells <- TRUE

# 2026b's transect sheets don't contain a date cell, so it's set here
# (taken from the workbook's own titles: "OPIHI DATA - 4/20/26 & 5/4/26").
b_transect_dates <- c("TRANSECT PT INTERCEPT (420)" = "2026-04-20",
                      "TRANSECT PT INTERCEPT (54)"  = "2026-05-04")
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---- Helpers ------------------------------------------------------
read_raw <- function(path, sheet) {
  # col_types = "list" keeps each cell's native type (dates, numbers, text)
  # range anchored at A1: by default read_excel() drops leading empty
  # rows/columns, which would shift every cell position (2026b's quadrat
  # sheet has an empty column A)
  read_excel(path, sheet = sheet, range = cell_limits(c(1, 1), c(NA, NA)),
             col_names = FALSE, col_types = "list", .name_repair = "minimal")
}

get_cell <- function(m, r, c) {
  if (r < 1 || c < 1 || r > nrow(m) || c > ncol(m)) return(NA)
  v <- m[[c]][[r]]
  if (is.null(v) || length(v) == 0) NA else v
}

clean_txt <- function(x) {
  # as.character() on a list turns blanks into the text "NA", so convert
  # element by element
  if (is.list(x)) {
    x <- map_chr(x, function(v) {
      if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v[1])) NA_character_ else as.character(v[1])
    })
  }
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", x)   # collapse spaces/newlines
  x <- trimws(x)
  x[x == ""] <- NA
  x
}

# Real dates only; anything else typed in a date cell (e.g. a name) -> NA
fmt_date <- function(x) if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) format(x, "%Y-%m-%d") else NA_character_
fmt_time <- function(x) if (inherits(x, "POSIXt")) format(x, "%H:%M") else clean_txt(x)
num <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))

col_vec <- function(m, rows, c) map(rows, ~ get_cell(m, .x, c))

# Column order of the final file
final_cols <- c("source_file", "sheet", "record_type", "date", "location",
                "data_entry_by", "group", "transect", "transect_point",
                "position_m", "quadrat_location_m", "category", "organism",
                "count", "quadrat_total_points", "notes")

# ---- 2026a / 2026c : Metadata sheet --------------------------------
read_metadata_ac <- function(path, sheet) {
  m <- read_raw(path, sheet)
  hdr <- map_chr(seq_len(ncol(m)), ~ clean_txt(get_cell(m, 1, .x)))
  keep <- which(!is.na(hdr))
  rows <- seq_len(nrow(m))[-1]
  cols <- map(keep, function(c) {
    map_chr(col_vec(m, rows, c), function(v) {
      if (inherits(v, "POSIXt")) {
        # times of day are stored on 1899-12-3x; real dates are 1950+
        if (as.integer(format(v, "%Y")) < 1950) format(v, "%H:%M") else format(v, "%Y-%m-%d")
      } else clean_txt(v)
    })
  })
  names(cols) <- hdr[keep]
  out <- as_tibble(cols, .name_repair = "minimal")
  # drop rows with no real content (template rows that only have a location)
  content <- out %>% select(-any_of(c("Location")))
  out <- out[rowSums(!is.na(content)) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  bind_cols(tibble(source_file = basename(path)), out)
}

# ---- 2026a / 2026c : Transect point intercept ----------------------
read_transect_ac <- function(path, sheet) {
  m <- read_raw(path, sheet)

  # Stop at the first stray template block pasted below the real data:
  # a row (after the header) whose column A holds text instead of a date.
  a <- col_vec(m, seq_len(nrow(m)), 1)
  stray <- which(seq_len(nrow(m)) > 1 &
                   map_lgl(a, ~ !is.na(.x) && !inherits(.x, "POSIXt")))
  last_row <- if (length(stray)) min(stray) - 1 else nrow(m)

  rows <- 2:last_row
  tibble(
    source_file    = basename(path),
    sheet          = sheet,
    record_type    = "transect_point",
    date           = map_chr(col_vec(m, rows, 1), fmt_date),
    location       = clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, 2)),
    data_entry_by  = clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, 3)),
    group          = NA_character_,
    transect       = num(col_vec(m, rows, 4)),
    transect_point = num(col_vec(m, rows, 5)),
    position_m     = num(col_vec(m, rows, 6)),
    quadrat_location_m   = NA_real_,
    category       = NA_character_,
    organism       = clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, 7)),
    count          = 1,
    quadrat_total_points = NA_real_,
    notes          = NA_character_
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(organism))          # template rows with no organism entered
}

# ---- 2026a / 2026c : Quadrat point counts --------------------------
read_quadrat_ac <- function(path, sheet) {
  m <- read_raw(path, sheet)

  cat_row <- 1; name_row <- 2; first_data <- 3
  hdr <- map_chr(seq_len(ncol(m)), ~ clean_txt(get_cell(m, name_row, .x)))

  total_col <- which(hdr == "Total Points")[1]
  notes_col <- which(grepl("^NOTES", hdr))[1]
  org_cols  <- which(seq_along(hdr) >= 7 & !is.na(hdr) &
                       seq_along(hdr) < total_col)

  # Category for each organism column: row 1 labels the first column of
  # each group (Limu (Algae), Blue-Green, Invertebrates, Substrate), and it
  # applies until the next label.
  cat_raw <- map_chr(seq_len(ncol(m)), ~ clean_txt(get_cell(m, cat_row, .x)))
  cat_fill <- cat_raw
  for (i in seq_along(cat_fill)) if (is.na(cat_fill[i]) && i > 1) cat_fill[i] <- cat_fill[i - 1]

  rows <- first_data:nrow(m)
  count_mat <- map(org_cols, ~ num(col_vec(m, rows, .x)))
  names(count_mat) <- org_cols
  has_data <- reduce(map(count_mat, ~ !is.na(.x)), `|`)   # row has >=1 count

  rows <- rows[has_data]
  if (length(rows) == 0) return(NULL)
  keep_idx <- which(has_data)

  base <- tibble(
    source_file    = basename(path),
    sheet          = sheet,
    record_type    = "quadrat_points",
    date           = map_chr(col_vec(m, rows, 1), fmt_date),
    location       = clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, 2)),
    data_entry_by  = clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, 3)),
    group          = NA_character_,
    transect       = num(col_vec(m, rows, 4)),
    transect_point = NA_real_,
    position_m     = NA_real_,
    quadrat_location_m   = num(col_vec(m, rows, 5)),
    quadrat_total_points = if (!is.na(total_col)) num(col_vec(m, rows, total_col)) else NA_real_,
    notes          = if (!is.na(notes_col)) clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, notes_col)) else NA_character_
  )

  map_dfr(seq_along(org_cols), function(k) {
    bind_cols(base,
              tibble(category = cat_fill[org_cols[k]],
                     organism = hdr[org_cols[k]],
                     count    = count_mat[[k]][keep_idx]))
  })
}

# ---- 2026b : transect point intercept (per group) -------------------
read_transect_b <- function(path, sheet) {
  m <- read_raw(path, sheet)

  title <- clean_txt(get_cell(m, 1, 1))
  loc <- if (!is.na(title) && grepl(" - ", title)) sub("^.* - ", "", title) else NA_character_

  # group columns: header row 4, columns C onward, stops at first blank header
  hdr <- map_chr(seq_len(ncol(m)), ~ clean_txt(get_cell(m, 4, .x)))
  gcols <- 3:(which(is.na(hdr) & seq_along(hdr) > 3)[1] - 1)
  group_label <- function(h) sub("^BLOCK ([0-9]+) GROUP ([0-9]+)$", "B\\1G\\2", h)
  names_row <- map_chr(seq_len(ncol(m)), ~ clean_txt(get_cell(m, 3, .x)))

  # data rows: every row from 5 down that has a point number. (Don't stop at
  # the first blank: the "(54)" sheet has 5 empty rows after point 30.)
  rows <- 5:nrow(m)
  rows <- rows[map_lgl(rows, ~ !is.na(num(get_cell(m, .x, 1))))]

  date_chr <- unname(b_transect_dates[sheet])

  map_dfr(gcols, function(c) {
    tibble(
      source_file    = basename(path),
      sheet          = sheet,
      record_type    = "transect_point",
      date           = date_chr,
      location       = loc,
      data_entry_by  = NA_character_,
      group          = group_label(hdr[c]),
      transect       = NA_real_,
      transect_point = num(col_vec(m, rows, 1)),
      position_m     = num(col_vec(m, rows, 2)),
      quadrat_location_m   = NA_real_,
      category       = NA_character_,
      organism       = clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, c)),
      count          = 1,
      quadrat_total_points = NA_real_,
      notes          = NA_character_
    )
  }) %>% filter(!is.na(organism))
}

# ---- 2026b : quadrat point intercept (group totals per date) --------
read_quadrat_b <- function(path, sheet) {
  m <- read_raw(path, sheet)

  # Dates sit in row 1 (one per block of group columns)
  date_cols <- which(map_lgl(seq_len(ncol(m)), ~ inherits(get_cell(m, 1, .x), "POSIXt")))
  date_cols <- date_cols[date_cols <= 11]       # ignore chart-helper cells to the right
  date_vals <- map_chr(date_cols, ~ fmt_date(get_cell(m, 1, .x)))

  # Group columns: row 2 has the group name (B4G1 ...); total columns are blank there
  grp <- map_chr(seq_len(ncol(m)), ~ clean_txt(get_cell(m, 2, .x)))
  gcols <- which(!is.na(grp) & seq_along(grp) >= 3 & seq_along(grp) <= 11)

  # Organism rows: below the "Organism/Substrate" header row until "TOTAL"
  hdr_row <- which(map_lgl(seq_len(nrow(m)),
                           ~ identical(clean_txt(get_cell(m, .x, 2)), "Organism/Substrate")))[1]
  if (is.na(hdr_row)) stop("Couldn't find the 'Organism/Substrate' header in column B of '", sheet, "'")
  r <- hdr_row + 1; rows <- integer(0)
  while (r <= nrow(m)) {
    lab <- clean_txt(get_cell(m, r, 2))
    if (is.na(lab) || grepl("^TOTAL", lab, ignore.case = TRUE)) break
    rows <- c(rows, r); r <- r + 1
  }

  map_dfr(gcols, function(c) {
    nearest <- date_cols[which.min(abs(date_cols - c))]
    entry   <- clean_txt(get_cell(m, 3, c))
    tibble(
      source_file    = basename(path),
      sheet          = sheet,
      record_type    = "quadrat_group_total",
      date           = date_vals[match(nearest, date_cols)],
      location       = NA_character_,
      data_entry_by  = entry,
      group          = grp[c],
      transect       = NA_real_,
      transect_point = NA_real_,
      position_m     = NA_real_,
      quadrat_location_m   = NA_real_,
      category       = NA_character_,
      organism       = clean_txt(col_vec(m, rows, 2)),
      count          = num(col_vec(m, rows, c)),
      quadrat_total_points = NA_real_,
      notes          = NA_character_
    )
  })
}

# ---- Run ----------------------------------------------------------
paths <- file.path(data_dir, files)
missing <- paths[!file.exists(paths)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Can't find: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))

data_parts <- list()
meta_parts <- list()

for (p in paths) {
  sheets <- excel_sheets(p)
  message("Reading ", basename(p), " [", paste(sheets, collapse = " | "), "]")

  if ("Metadata" %in% sheets) {
    # 2026a / 2026c template
    t_sheet <- sheets[grepl("^Transect", sheets)][1]
    q_sheet <- sheets[grepl("^Quadrat", sheets)][1]
    meta_parts[[p]] <- read_metadata_ac(p, "Metadata")
    data_parts[[paste(p, "T")]] <- read_transect_ac(p, t_sheet)
    data_parts[[paste(p, "Q")]] <- read_quadrat_ac(p, q_sheet)
  } else if ("QUADRAT PT INTERCEPT" %in% sheets) {
    # 2026b class workbook
    for (s in sheets[grepl("^TRANSECT PT INTERCEPT", sheets)])
      data_parts[[paste(p, s)]] <- read_transect_b(p, s)
    data_parts[[paste(p, "Q")]] <- read_quadrat_b(p, "QUADRAT PT INTERCEPT")
  } else {
    warning("Unrecognized layout, skipped: ", basename(p))
  }
}

combined <- bind_rows(data_parts) %>% select(all_of(final_cols))

# Blank-cell handling applies to quadrat rows only (transect rows are always hits)
is_quad <- combined$record_type != "transect_point"
if (drop_empty_cells) {
  combined <- combined[!(is_quad & is.na(combined$count)), ]
} else {
  combined$count[is_quad & is.na(combined$count)] <- 0
}

combined <- arrange(combined, source_file, record_type, date, location, group,
                    transect, transect_point, quadrat_location_m, organism)

write_csv(combined, out_file, na = "")
message("Wrote ", nrow(combined), " rows x ", ncol(combined), " columns to ", out_file)

metadata <- bind_rows(meta_parts)
if (nrow(metadata) > 0) {
  write_csv(metadata, meta_file, na = "")
  message("Wrote ", nrow(metadata), " survey rows to ", meta_file)
}
```

**How the merge works**

- **Ties:** if a data row matches several metadata rows, the one sharing the most names wins. If it's still tied, the row stays unmerged and is flagged `ambiguous` instead of guessing.

- **Report:** when it finishes, it prints the match counts, the date and name combinations that didn't merge, and any metadata rows that no data matched.
- **Full names:** because spaces count as separators, a full name like "Mary Smith" becomes two names, and either one can trigger a match.

- **Metadata column names:** these are matched ignoring case, spaces and symbols, so `Team Leader`, `team_leader` and `Team.Leader` all work. In the output they get the `meta_` prefix, like `meta_team_leader`.

```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# merge_metadata_data.R
#
# Merges a metadata data frame into a data data frame, both already
# loaded in your R session (e.g. after your own manual cleaning).
#
# A data row is matched to a metadata row when
#   1. the date is EXACTLY the same (data `date` = metadata `Date`), AND
#   2. at least one name in the data's `data_entry_by` also appears in the
#      metadata's `Team Leader` or `Team Members`.
#
# Names are compared after splitting each cell into individual names
# (separators: comma, space, semicolon, "&", "/", and the word "and"),
# ignoring upper/lower case and stray punctuation. So "Ann, Bob",
# "Ann Bob" and "ann bob" all give the names {ann, bob}.
#
# NOTE: because spaces count as separators, a full name such as "Mary Smith"
# is treated as two names, "mary" and "smith", and EITHER one can trigger a
# match.
#
# If one data row matches several metadata rows (same date, shared names),
# the metadata row sharing the MOST names wins. If that is still a tie the
# row is left unmerged and flagged "ambiguous" rather than guessing.
#
# Every data row is kept. Rows with no match get blank metadata columns.
# Three columns are added to show what happened:
#   match_status   matched | no_match | ambiguous | no_date | no_name
#   matched_names  the names that matched (for checking)
#   metadata_row   row number of the metadata data frame that was merged
#
# What the two input data frames need:
#   data:  columns `date`, `data_entry_by`, and `source_file`*
#   meta:  columns `Date`, `Team Leader`, `Team Members`, and `source_file`*
#          (metadata column names are matched ignoring case/spaces/symbols,
#          so "Team Leader", "team_leader" and "Team.Leader" all work)
#   * source_file is only needed if require_same_source_file = TRUE
#   Date columns can be text ("2026-01-24") or real Date/POSIXct values;
#   they are compared as yyyy-mm-dd text, and `date` comes back as text.
#
# Requires: dplyr, tidyr, purrr, readr, tibble
#   install.packages(c("dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "readr", "tibble"))
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)

# ---- Helpers ------------------------------------------------------

# Split name cells into individual, normalised names
tokenize <- function(...) {
  x <- unlist(lapply(list(...), as.character))
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(character(0))
  tok <- unlist(strsplit(tolower(x), "[[:space:],;&/]+"))
  tok <- gsub("^[[:punct:]]+|[[:punct:]]+$", "", tok)   # stray punctuation
  tok <- tok[tok != "" & tok != "and"]
  unique(tok)
}

# Dates (text, Date or POSIXct) -> "yyyy-mm-dd" text; blanks -> NA
as_date_chr <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, c("Date", "POSIXt"))) x <- format(x, "%Y-%m-%d")
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x[x == ""] <- NA_character_
  x
}

# ---- The merge ----------------------------------------------------
merge_metadata_data <- function(data, meta, require_same_source_file = TRUE) {

  data <- as_tibble(data)
  meta <- as_tibble(meta)

  # Normalise metadata column names: "Team Leader" -> team_leader, etc.
  nm <- tolower(names(meta))
  nm <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", nm)
  names(meta) <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", nm)
  if (anyDuplicated(names(meta)))
    stop("Metadata has columns whose names become identical after cleaning: ",
         paste(names(meta)[duplicated(names(meta))], collapse = ", "))

  # Check required columns
  miss_meta <- setdiff(c("date", "team_leader", "team_members"), names(meta))
  if (length(miss_meta))
    stop("Metadata is missing column(s): ", paste(miss_meta, collapse = ", "))
  miss_data <- setdiff(c("date", "data_entry_by"), names(data))
  if (length(miss_data))
    stop("Data is missing column(s): ", paste(miss_data, collapse = ", "))
  if (require_same_source_file &&
      !("source_file" %in% names(data) && "source_file" %in% names(meta)))
    stop("Both data frames need a `source_file` column when ",
         "require_same_source_file = TRUE (or set it to FALSE).")

  # Helper columns (removed again at the end)
  data$date      <- as_date_chr(data$date)
  meta$date      <- as_date_chr(meta$date)
  data$.data_row <- seq_len(nrow(data))
  meta$.meta_id  <- seq_len(nrow(meta))
  data$.src <- if (require_same_source_file) as.character(data$source_file) else "all"
  meta$.src <- if (require_same_source_file) as.character(meta$source_file) else "all"

  # One row per (metadata row, name)
  meta_names <- meta %>%
    transmute(.meta_id, .src, date,
              name = map2(team_leader, team_members, tokenize)) %>%
    unnest(name)

  # One row per (distinct file + date + data_entry_by, name)
  keys <- data %>%
    distinct(.src, date, data_entry_by) %>%
    mutate(key_id = row_number(),
           name   = map(data_entry_by, tokenize))

  key_names <- keys %>%
    select(key_id, .src, date, name) %>%
    unnest(name)

  # Same date (and file) + at least one shared name
  hits <- as_tibble(merge(as.data.frame(key_names), as.data.frame(meta_names),
                          by = c(".src", "date", "name")))

  pairs <- hits %>%
    group_by(key_id, .meta_id) %>%
    summarise(n_names       = n_distinct(name),
              matched_names = paste(sort(unique(name)), collapse = ", "),
              .groups = "drop")

  # Keep the metadata row(s) sharing the most names, then decide
  key_match <- pairs %>%
    group_by(key_id) %>%
    filter(n_names == max(n_names)) %>%
    summarise(n_candidates  = n(),
              metadata_row  = if (n() == 1) .meta_id else NA_integer_,
              matched_names = if (n() == 1) matched_names else NA_character_,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(match_status = if_else(n_candidates == 1, "matched", "ambiguous"))

  keys <- keys %>%
    left_join(key_match, by = "key_id") %>%
    mutate(match_status = case_when(
      is.na(date)                               ~ "no_date",
      is.na(data_entry_by) | lengths(name) == 0 ~ "no_name",
      !is.na(match_status)                      ~ match_status,
      TRUE                                      ~ "no_match"
    ))

  # Metadata columns to attach (prefixed meta_)
  meta_out <- meta %>% select(-date, -.src)
  if (require_same_source_file) meta_out <- meta_out %>% select(-source_file)
  meta_out <- meta_out %>% rename_with(~ paste0("meta_", .x), -.meta_id)

  result <- data %>%
    left_join(keys %>% select(.src, date, data_entry_by,
                              match_status, matched_names, metadata_row),
              by = c(".src", "date", "data_entry_by")) %>%
    left_join(meta_out, by = c("metadata_row" = ".meta_id")) %>%
    arrange(.data_row) %>%
    select(-.data_row, -.src)

  # ---- Report ----
  message("\nMatch results (data rows):")
  print(count(result, match_status, name = "rows"))

  unmatched <- result %>%
    filter(match_status != "matched") %>%
    count(across(any_of(c("source_file", "date", "data_entry_by", "match_status"))),
          name = "rows")
  if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
    message("\nData that did NOT merge (check these dates/names):")
    print(unmatched, n = Inf)
  }

  unused <- meta %>%
    filter(!.meta_id %in% result$metadata_row) %>%
    select(metadata_row = .meta_id,
           any_of(c("source_file", "date", "location", "team_leader", "team_members")))
  if (nrow(unused) > 0) {
    message("\nMetadata rows that no data matched:")
    print(unused, n = Inf)
  }

  result
}

# ---- Use it -------------------------------------------------------
# Put the names of YOUR cleaned data frames on the right-hand side:
data_name <- "filtered_data2"  # the observations (one row per record)
meta_name <- "filtered_metadata2"  # the metadata (one row per survey)

if (!exists(data_name) || !exists(meta_name))
  stop("Can't find `", data_name, "` and/or `", meta_name, "` in your R session. ",
       "Edit data_name / meta_name above to match your data frames' names.")
data_in <- get(data_name)
meta_in <- get(meta_name)

merged_data <- merge_metadata_data(data_in, meta_in,
                                   require_same_source_file = TRUE)

# Optional: also save it
write_csv(merged_data, here("OPIHI_Project", "Outputs","combined_data2_with_metadata.csv"), na = "")
message("\nResult is in `merged_data` (", nrow(merged_data), " rows x ",
        ncol(merged_data), " columns); also saved to combined_data2_with_metadata.csv")

```

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## AI Chat Log - Template

**Kat:**

I now have a .csv file with a few redundant columns. Write me an R script that joins certain columns together into one column containing the information of both, excluding NA values. The columns I would like to join are: 

"notes" and "meta_notes" (just call this combined column "notes")

**Claude:**

I've written `join_columns.R`, which merges `notes` and `meta_notes` into a single `notes` column. I haven't run it in R, so it's untested.

**How it handles each row**
- If both columns have text, they're joined with `"; "` between them (for example `"A; B"`).
- If only one has text, that text is used as is.
- If neither has text, the result stays blank.
- If both hold identical text, it's kept once rather than repeated.
- NA and empty cells are ignored, and extra spaces are trimmed.

The combined `notes` column sits where the original `notes` column was, and `meta_notes` is removed. Other columns are untouched. The script prints how many rows had a value in both columns, so you can see how many were actually combined.

**Before running it:** at the top of the script, set `in_file` to your .csv's name. It defaults to `combined_data2_with_metadata.csv`. The result is written to `combined_data2_joined.csv`, and you can change that name in the settings too. You can also change `separator` if you'd rather use something other than `"; "`.

To join other redundant columns later, add a line to the `joins` list. For example, `location = c("location", "meta_location")` would merge those two into one `location` column.

:::



```{r}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# join_columns.R
#
# Joins redundant columns into one column that holds the information from
# all of them, leaving out NA/blank values. Here: "notes" + "meta_notes"
# -> "notes".
#
#   notes        meta_notes     ->  notes
#   "A"          "B"                "A; B"
#   "A"          NA                 "A"
#   NA           "B"                "B"
#   NA           NA                 NA
#   "A"          "A"                "A"      (identical text is kept once)
#
# The combined column takes the position of the first column joined, and
# the other original columns are removed.
#
# To join more columns later, add another line to `joins`, e.g.
#   joins <- list(notes = c("notes", "meta_notes"),
#                 location = c("location", "meta_location"))
#
# Requires: readr, purrr
#   install.packages(c("readr", "purrr"))
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

library(readr)
library(purrr)

# ---- Settings -----------------------------------------------------
in_file   <- here("OPIHI_Project", "Outputs", "alldata_4_5_8_26_combined.csv")   # your .csv file
out_file  <- here("OPIHI_Project", "Outputs", "alldata_joinedcol.csv")
separator <- "; "                                 # put between joined values

# new column name = the columns to join into it
joins <- list(
  notes = c("notes", "meta_notes"),
  location = c("location", "meta_location")
)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# Read everything as text so no values get altered
df <- read_csv(in_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
               na = c("", "NA"), progress = FALSE)

join_columns <- function(df, new_name, cols, sep) {
  missing <- setdiff(cols, names(df))
  if (length(missing))
    stop("Column(s) not found in the file: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))

  # Combine each row's non-NA, non-blank values (identical values kept once)
  combined <- pmap_chr(df[cols], function(...) {
    v <- trimws(c(...))
    v <- unique(v[!is.na(v) & v != ""])
    if (length(v) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(v, collapse = sep)
  })

  # Where the new column goes: the position of the first column joined
  pos   <- min(match(cols, names(df)))
  keep  <- setdiff(names(df), cols)
  order <- append(keep, new_name, after = pos - 1)

  n_both <- sum(rowSums(!is.na(df[cols]) & trimws(as.matrix(df[cols])) != "") > 1,
                na.rm = TRUE)
  message("'", new_name, "': joined ", paste(cols, collapse = " + "), " (",
          n_both, " rows had a value in more than one of them)")

  df[[new_name]] <- combined
  df[order]
}

for (nm in names(joins)) {
  df <- join_columns(df, nm, joins[[nm]], separator)
}

write_csv(df, out_file, na = "")
message("Wrote ", nrow(df), " rows x ", ncol(df), " columns to ", out_file)

```
